summary:
The "Shelter Moon to Home" project is an innovative initiative developed to address the challenges of sustainable living, resource management, and extreme environmental adaptation, bridging space exploration concepts with terrestrial housing needs. Inspired by lunar architecture and survival strategies, we developed a conceptual and technological framework designed to create resilient, eco-friendly, and self-sufficient habitats.
​This project addresses the challenge of housing scarcity and climate vulnerability by utilizing advanced materials and smart resource utilization techniques derived from space missions. It is crucial because as climate change intensifies and space exploration advances, we must design modular, highly efficient shelters capable of protecting human life in harsh conditions—whether on the Moon or in disaster-stricken areas on Earth. Our solution integrates cutting-edge design to ensure safety, durability, and a sustainable path forward for future communities.
details:
​What it does & How it works:

The "Shelter Moon to Home" project functions as an innovative architectural and technological framework inspired by lunar exploration. It works by adapting space-grade survival strategies, modular engineering, and self-sufficient resource utilization techniques to design resilient habitats that can withstand extreme environments.

​Benefits & Intended Impact:

The primary benefit is providing safe, durable, and sustainable housing solutions. Its intended impact is to protect human lives against climate vulnerability and housing scarcity, offering adaptable shelter systems for both extreme off-world environments (like the Moon) and disaster-stricken areas on Earth.

​Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Used:

​Software & Design: CAD software for structural modeling, simulation tools for environmental stress testing.

​Technologies: Conceptual frameworks integrating IoT for smart resource monitoring and eco-friendly material analysis.

​Creativity & Factors Considered:

The project is creative because it bridges two distant domains: space exploration and terrestrial housing. Our team considered energy efficiency, structural resilience under harsh conditions, scalability, and the psychological well-being of inhabitants in enclosed, modular spaces.
